component.name: Gear Lever COSMIC
component.summary: Add AppImages to your app menu and keep them updated

description.p: Add AppImages to your app menu, keep them updated, and see clearly what can and cannot be updated. Inspired by Gear Lever and rewritten in Rust with libcosmic.

Updates replace the file in place, so running apps keep working and switch to the new version when they restart. Versions are read from the AppImage itself, menu entries are refreshed when an app updated itself, and apps with their own updater are labelled as such. It also checks whether an AppImage can start on this system (FUSE 2 or FUSE 3, missing libraries).
A command line tool with typed commands, dry-run plans and live window controls makes everything usable by scripts and AI agents.

AppImages whose file name still carries a version (such as App-1.2-x86_64.appimage) can be given their standard name with one click ("Use Standard Name") or app.rename-file, together with their menu entry and icon, even while they run. Help, guide and docs now show the command that actually starts the CLI, such as the AppImage's full path followed by cli. Apps started with Launch no longer hang: their output goes to a log file (~/.local/share/gearlever-cosmic/launch-logs) instead of a pipe that closed once the launcher returned, which stopped Electron apps such as ZCode from loading. The AppImage no longer bundles unrelated system data, and it can be built on any common Linux distribution.

Faster and lighter: command-line output can be captured in 0.2 s instead of 6 s, the window uses about 40% less memory than before, AppImages built with current DwarFS tools (including this one) are read correctly, and refreshing a menu entry restores missing details such as the window icon match.

First release: Gear Lever's features in a native COSMIC app, in-place updates of running apps, honest update statuses, versions read from the file (Gear Lever issue #497), system requirement checks, custom icons that survive updates, and an agent CLI.
